UAE Implements Sweeping Lockdowns Amid Respiratory Virus Surge, Disrupting Economic Activity

Abu Dhabi/Dubai – The United Arab Emirates has imposed strict nationwide lockdowns and business closures in response to a rapidly spreading respiratory virus, halting much of the country’s economic activity and straining supply chains, government and industry sources said on Thursday.

Schools, shopping malls, entertainment venues, and non-essential businesses have been ordered closed since Tuesday, while movement between emirates is being heavily restricted. Only essential services, such as pharmacies and supermarkets, remain open under reduced hours. The Ministry of Health and Prevention reported over 7,800 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of active infections to 49,000.

Authorities say the measures are necessary to contain the epidemic, which has caused a surge in hospital admissions, particularly in Dubai and Sharjah. “The health and safety of our citizens and residents is our top priority,” Health Minister Dr. Layla Al Qasimi said at a press conference. “We urge everyone to comply with the restrictions and limit unnecessary movement.”

Economic repercussions have been swift, with the Emirates Business Council estimating daily losses at over 1.2 billion dirhams ($327 million) across sectors. PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp, which provides technical support for oilfield projects in the UAE, confirmed that its operations have been “significantly disrupted” due to travel bans and site closures. “We are working closely with local authorities and partners to ensure the safety of our teams and resume critical activities as soon as permitted,” a company spokesperson said.

Analysts warn that extended lockdowns could have a ripple effect across the Gulf, given the UAE’s role as a major regional transport and trade hub. “The impact on logistics, energy, and construction is particularly severe,” said Omar Faris, senior economist at the Dubai Policy Institute. “Many companies are facing delays in project timelines and challenges in workforce mobility.”

Officials have not indicated when restrictions may be lifted, saying the situation is under constant review. The UAE government has urged the public to follow all health directives and avoid public gatherings until further notice.
